recorded.prompt:q-pinning:a: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-pinning:a: an independent reader (19-concurrency-pitfalls q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-pinning:a: ruled out: The page's PinningExample shows blocking I/O inside synchronized succeeding without an exception: "synchronized (lock) { String data = fetchFromDb(); // Blocking I/O while pinned -- carrier is stuck! ... }" -- no exception is thrown.
recorded.prompt:q-pinning:b: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-pinning:b: an independent reader (19-concurrency-pitfalls q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-pinning:b: ruled out: The page states the opposite: "when a virtual thread enters a synchronized block ... it 'pins' itself to the carrier thread. While pinned: The virtual thread cannot unmount. The carrier thread is blocked along with the virtual thread."
recorded.prompt:q-starvation:b: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-starvation:b: an independent reader (19-concurrency-pitfalls q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-starvation:b: ruled out: The page says the default (non-fair) lock lets readers, not writers, go first: "The default ReentrantReadWriteLock is non-fair, which can cause writer starvation under high read contention (readers keep acquiring the read lock, preventing writers from ever acquiring the write lock)."
recorded.prompt:q-starvation:c: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-starvation:c: an independent reader (19-concurrency-pitfalls q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-starvation:c: ruled out: The page says the write lock is exclusive of readers: "Only one thread can hold the write lock, and it requires exclusive access (no concurrent readers or writers)."
